document.about: Reproductive Health (2018) 15:146, 'Trends in adolescent first births in five countries in Latin America and the Caribbean: disaggregated data from demographic and health surveys', PMC6114051. Its Table 3 (p5) is set in five country blocks: each block's title (`Bolivia 1994 | Bolivia 2008 | % point change | …`, `Colombia 1990 | Colombia 2010 | …`) over the same line of column names (`<16 | 16/17 | 18/19 | <20` twice, then `<20`) and three rows. The PDF is linked from the PMC article page; PMC refuses scripted downloads.

notes: 2026-11-25 (restated blocks, from #351's audit): each block was read as a table of its own, its title as the header and its column line as the first row of data. The blocks are now one table: each title a section over its block's rows and each column line a restated header for them. With the first title over the first column line, the table has no header rows, so no block is named by another's title.
2026-11-26 (#346): the first block's title line writes no spaces, and its `<20` stands a word space from `change`; it now reads `rate of change < 20`, the section label with it.

checks.issue: Restated blocks: the column line was a row of data, and `34.0` was named by nothing.
